outside_audits.note: The two most serious findings in the 1.0.3 regression audits: the Defense lane's hard clearance branch dropped cleared buyers from cleared roles, and reports on a non-Gmail route could be recorded as sent before delivery. Both were fixed in 1.0.4 (2026-11-18). If you find audit criticism of this product, check the version it names against the current version in product.json before weighing it.

purpose: Corroboration for the product record at product.json: two real testers' runs with their outcomes, their verbatim testimonials, and the outside audit history. These are dated records of what happened, not promises of what a buyer's fleet will do. A buyer's numbers depend on their own resume and market.

testimonial.attribution: Derek, the first user of My Job Fleet. Verbatim and unedited.
testimonial.text:
I used to run my own job applications by hand in Muse AI, so I was already sold on the idea. Then Samuel showed me his job fleet, and I saw my way was the Flintstones and his was the Jetsons.

I got the full replica. It watches 1,566 companies for me across the different job sites, which I could never have set up or maintained on my own. In one run it read 470 postings in full and only 8 were worth my time. It has sent applications for me to Delinea, Dropbox, and Palo Alto Networks. Palo Alto is under review right now.

The best part is what it caught in my own resume. I had written that I had Kubernetes experience in production. I hadn't. The system flagged it and I corrected it. That alone was worth it to me.

testimonial.attribution: Jude, a My Job Fleet user. Verbatim and unedited.
testimonial.text: I used Muse to run my insider-risk job search like a system, not a scramble. It verified roles on employer sites, kept my applications honest to my résumé, tracked every submission with proof, and only moved roles forward when the employer actually responded. That process got me to interview stage with Saronic and Experian — including a hiring-manager interview already scheduled. The biggest difference was clarity: I always knew what was submitted, what was still draft, and what needed my decision next.
